newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court's jurisdiction in preliminary ruling is limited.
newsitem.headline: Court's jurisdiction in preliminary ruling is limited.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday Community rules on employment do not apply to labour disputes between two groups from the same member state.
An Italian court asked whether Italian labour law governing mediation should be set aside as incompatible with EC treaty articles 48, 49, 54 and 90.
The court said it does not have jurisdiction, within the framework of an article 177 reference for a preliminary ruling, to decide if a national measure is compatible with EU law.

"The court has no jurisdiction to give a preliminary ruling on a question submitted by a national court where it is quite obvious that the interpretation of Community law sought by that court bears no relation to the actual facts of the main action..." the court said.

The court found that the supply of services by an Italian cooperative, to an Italian public body "has no connection whatsoever with any of the situations envisaged by Community law in the area of freedom of movement for persons and services."
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
Reference from the Pretura Circondale, Biella (Italy) for a preliminary ruling between
Unita Socio-Sanitaria Locale No 47 di Biella (USSL)
Istituto Nazionale per l'Assicurazione contro gli Infortuni sul Lavoro (INAIL)
on the interpretation of articles 48, 49, 54 and 90 of the EC Treaty
Articles 48, 52, and 59 of the EC Treaty do not apply to a situation which is confined in all respects within a member state.
